BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION

 IN THE MATTER OF SOUTHWESTERN                           )
 PUBLIC       SERVICE       COMPANY’S                    )
 APPLICATION FOR: (1) REVISION OF ITS                    )      Docket No. 25-00079-UT
 RETAIL RATES UNDER ADVICE NOTICE 341;                   )
 AND (2) OTHER ASSOCIATED RELIEF                         )


                                         PROCEDRAL ORDER

       THIS MATTER comes before Christopher P. Ryan and Patrick C. Schaefer, hearing

examiners for the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission, following the prehearing

conference held on December 12, 2025, at which a procedural schedule and other matters were

discussed. The hearing examiners FIND and CONCLUDE as follows.

       1.      On November 20, 2025, Southwestern Public Service Company (SPS) filed its

application requesting Commission authorization to revise its retail rates under Advice Notice No.

341.

       2.      The Commission aspires to issue a final order on SPS’s application in the nine

months and thirty-days permitted by statute. 1 A nine-month suspension period from December

20, 2025, produces a deadline of September 20, 2026. This means the Commission must issue a

final order at the scheduled open meeting on September 10, 2026.

       3.      On Tuesday, November 25, 2025, the Commission issued an order appointing the

hearing examiners named above to preside over this matter.

       4.      On Monday, December 8, 2025, the hearing examiners scheduled a prehearing

conference for Friday, December 12, 2023, to create a procedural schedule for the adjudication.

Prior to the prehearing, the hearing examiners circulated a proposed procedural schedule by e-mail



1 NMSA 1978, §§ 62-8-7(B), (C) (2011).
                 BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Procedural Order                                                            Docket No. 25-00079-UT



that reflected the Commission’s final-order-target date of September 10, 2026. All procedural

events preceding the intended date for issuance of a final order necessarily turn on and are

dependent on the Commission’s objectives regarding the desired case-completion date.

       5.      On December 11, 2025, the Commission issued an order suspending the revised

rates proposed by SPS in Advice Notice No. 341 for a period of nine months beginning December

20, 2025. Nine months from that date is, as noted already, September 20, 2026.

       6.      The prehearing conference on December 12, 2025, was attended by counsel from

SPS, staff of the Commission’s Utility Division, the New Mexico Department of Justice, the New

Mexico Large Customer Group, Occidental Permian Ltd., the Coalition for Clean Affordable

Energy, Prosperity Works, Louisiana Energy Services, and the Federal Executive Agencies.

       7.      All contributed to and were given opportunity to participate in the creation of the

procedural schedule. That schedule along with the other matters discussed at the prehearing are

adopted as ordered below.

       IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED:

       A.      As soon as practicable, but no later than February 2, 2026, SPS shall (at its sole

expense) (1) mail the approved notice attached here as Attachment A to customers by bill stuffer

or email (if the customer has enrolled in electronic/digital billing); (2) publish the notice once in

newspapers of general circulation in every county where SPS provides service in New Mexico.

       B.      As soon as practicable, SPS shall post the approved notice on its website in a

location that is maximally visible to customers and likely to be seen by them.

       C.      SPS shall utilize social media to the maximum extent practicable to alert its

customers to the existence of this proceeding and the rates proposed. To the extent social media

requires modification to the approved notice or only a link to that notice, this is approved.
                                                    -2-
                   BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Procedural Order                                                                        Docket No. 25-00079-UT



        D.       SPS shall file promptly in this docket an affidavit confirming it completed the forms

of mailing, publication, and posting identified above.

        E.       Person desiring to intervene in this case must file a motion to intervene that

conforms to 1.2.2.23(A) and 1.2.2.23(B) NMAC on or before February 12, 2026.

        F.       Any dispositive motion—a motion to dismiss, any motion that would (as a matter

of law) resolve some portion of this case or require the applicant to retract and refile the

application, or any motion that would result in summary rejection of any portion of the

application—must be filed on or before February 27, 2026. 2 This dispositive motion deadline is

established to ensure the proceedings are efficient and that any energy dedicated to establishing

the application is patently deficient in some way is expended early in the proceedings before the

case turns to competing evidence of what constitutes the most optimal outcome.

        G.       A public comment session will be conducted at a time and place that will be

determined by the Commission. The date and time will be announced on the Commission’s

website. Persons interested in this case may submit oral or written comments as permitted by

1.2.2.23(F) NMAC at times other than the public comment session, including at any of the

Commission’s regular open meetings.



2 At the prehearing, several intervenors correctly pointed out that the rule governing motions to dismiss states

that a party may file such a motion “at any time.” 1.2.2.12(B) NMAC. This direction is seemingly at odds with
another provision in a different but applicable section of the administrative code which states that, “[i]n the
event” a rate filing is found to be incomplete, “the Commission shall advise the filing utility of the deficiency of
the filing within thirty (30) days of receipt and will hold the Rates, Rules, or Forms for a reasonable time until
the additional information required or necessary corrections have been provided.” 17.1.210.11(F). The exact
meaning and significance of the latter provisions is unclear, but it seems generally at odds with the notion that a
motion to dismiss for evidentiary insufficiency should and may come at any time. The purpose of imposing a
dispositive motion deadline early in the case is simply to prevent a circumstance where dismissal occurs late in
the proceedings after all case participants including the Commission have expended resources shepherding it
through the process. The Commission is a resource constrained entity and must design processes to maximize
the impact of those constrained resources.
                                                             -3-
                 BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Procedural Order                                                            Docket No. 25-00079-UT



       H.      If the parties believe that a stipulation can be reached, they are encouraged to find

ways to achieve that end as early as possible in these proceedings. If a stipulation is reached, a

prehearing conference will be promptly scheduled and an alternative procedural schedule for

hearing on a stipulation set.

       I.      Staff and intervenor direct testimony shall be filed on or before March 27, 2026.

       J.      Rebuttal testimony shall be filed by April 17, 2026.

       K.      The public hearing will begin at 9 a.m. on May 26, 2026, and will continue through

each succeeding business day until June 5, 2026. If additional hearing days are required, they will

continue on June 8, 2026, and until the hearing is complete.

       L.      Person filing prepared testimony consistent with 1.2.2.35(I) NMAC on behalf of a

party shall attend the hearing and submit to examination under oath.

       M.      All parties must file all case documents through the Commission’s electronic filing

service. The Commission will be adopting a new filing system during the time anticipated for this

proceeding. If there are questions regarding filing with the Commission, those should be sent to

the Records Management Bureau at prc.records@prc.nm.gov or the Consumers Relations Bureau

at 1-888-427-5772.

       N.      The Application and supporting documents are accessible online on SPS’s website,

https://www.xcelenergy.com/company/rates_and_regulations/filings , and at www.prc.nm.gov , e-

Docket-Case Lookup, Case No. 25-00079.

       O.      Any interested person may examine SPS’s application and supporting documents

and other documents filed in the public record of this case on the Commission’s docketing system

or SPS’s website: https://www.xcelenergy.com/company/rates_and_regulations/rates/rate_cases.


                                                    -4-
                 BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Procedural Order                                                            Docket No. 25-00079-UT



       P.      The procedural dates and requirements set out here are subject to change. Hearings

are occasionally rescheduled or canceled.

       Q.      The Commission’s rules of procedure, 1.2.2.1 NMAC et seq., shall apply in this

case except as modified by order of the hearing examiners or Commission. The rules of procedure

and other Commission rules are available online at the New Mexico Compilation Commission at

https://www.srca.nm.gov/nmac-home/nmac-titles/ .

       R.      Discovery matters and disputes shall be governed by the Commission’s discovery

rules at 1.2.2.25 NMAC. Agreements between or among any of the participants regarding

discovery matters is encouraged. All other participants shall be notified of such agreements.

Motions regarding discovery disputes will not be considered unless accompanied by a statement

that the participants made a good faith effort to resolve the dispute but were unable to do so.

       ISSUED under the Seal of the Commission at Santa Fe, New Mexico this 15th day of

December 2025.

       NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION



                                       ___________________________
                                       Patrick C. Schaefer
                                       Hearing Examiner



                                      ___________________________
                                      Christopher P. Ryan
                                      Hearing Examiner




                                                    -5-
                                                                            COMMISSIONERS
                                                                           GABRIEL AGUILERA
                                                                           GREG NIBERT
                                                                           PATRICK O’CONNELL


                      NOTICE TO SPS CUSTOMERS
SPS (Southwestern Public Service Company) has ﬁled with the Commission an Application
requesting approval of revised New Mexico retail electric rates under NMSA 1978, §§ 62-8-7,
62-3-3(P), and 62-6-14(D) of the Public Utility Act, and Sections 17.1.3 (the “Future Test Year
Rule”) and 17.9.530 (“Rule 530”) of the New Mexico Administrative Code (“NMAC”), and for
other approvals and authorizations described in the Application. (PRC Case No. 25-00079-
UT). The revised rates, set forth in Advice Notice No. 341, would increase SPS’s estimated
revenue requirement for New Mexico by $175,354,544.

Details of SPS’s Application are provided in the next paragraphs.

The Application and supporting documents and other documents are accessible online on
SPS’s website, https://www.xcelenergy.com/company/rates_and_regulations/filings, and
at www.prc.nm.gov, e-Docket-Case Lookup, Case No. 25-00079-UT.

     NO ACTION ON YOUR PART IS REQUIRED UNLESS YOU WANT TO
  INTERVENE AS A PARTY OR PROVIDE COMMENT ON THE APPLICATION

The major events for public participation in this matter will occur as follows:

             Deadline for motions to intervene to become a party: February 12, 2026
             Deadline for Intervenors’ direct testimony: March 27, 2026
             Deadline for rebuttal testimony: April 17, 2026
             Public Evidentiary Hearing: May 26, 2026 - June 5, 2026

THESE ARE NOT THE ONLY DEADLINES, AND POTENTIAL INTERVENORS ARE ADVISED
TO READ THE COMPLETE PROCEDURAL ORDER ISSUED ON DECEMBER 15, 2025.

While there is no set deadline for public comment, we encourage the public to provide
comments at their earliest convenience, prior to the conclusion of the case. More details on
providing comment and about the public hearing appear on the last page of this document.

How to Intervene (Follow Rule 1.2.2.23 (A ) & (B) NMAC). If you wish to become a party to
this case, you must file a motion for leave to intervene.


                                              -1-
 For filing with the Commission (Follow Rule 1.2.2.10 -12 NMAC). All filings must comply
with the Commission’s electronic filing requirements. For questions or for more
information, contact the prc.records@prc.nm.gov or Consumers Relations Bureau at 1-
888-427-5772.

The Rules of Procedure cited above are found at https://srca.nm.gov/nmac-home/nmac-
titles/. The rules are subject to modifications by the Commission or Hearing Examiners.

SPS’s Application asks the Commission to:

   1. Authorize SPS to increase its base rate charges for the New Mexico retail jurisdiction
      by $175,354,544, a 24.25% increase over current base rate revenue and 16.73% in
      total revenues, using: a base period of July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2025 (“Base
      Period”); a linkage data timeframe of July 1, 2025 through November 30, 2026
      (“Linkage Data Timeframe”); and a future test year of December 1, 2026 through
      November 30, 2027 (“Future Test Year”); a New Mexico retail base rate revenue
      requirement of $892,652,373; a return on equity (“ROE”) of 10.5%, a 56% equity ratio,
      and a 5.29% cost of debt; and an overall weighted average cost of capital (“WACC”)
      of 8.21%;
   2. Approve SPS’s request to include in rate base the capital investment SPS has placed
      in service or will place in service during the Base Period, Linkage Data Timeframe, and
      Future Test Year;
   3. Authorize SPS to include in rate base new renewable generation and storage projects
      that will enter service during the Future Test Year, including those approved in Case
      No. 23-00252-UT: Plant X Solar, Cunningham I Solar, Cunningham II Solar, and
      Cunningham Battery Energy Storage System (“BESS”); and the Plant X BESS proposed
      in Case No. 25-00066-UT;
   4. Authorize a fair return on and recovery of SPS’s investment in those facilities;
   5. Approve updated depreciation rates, including depreciation rates that reﬂect
      extended service lives for speciﬁed generation units;
   6. Approve SPS’s proposed change in authorized equity percentage and capital
      structure;
   7. Allow SPS to recover reasonable operating and administrative expenses, including
      corporate operation and maintenance (“O&M”) costs, professional dues, community
      contributions, and rate-case and other regulatory expenses;
   8. Authorize SPS to assign all Cunningham BESS costs to New Mexico retail customers;
   9. Approve SPS’s proposed treatment of federal tax-credit beneﬁts, including:


                                            -2-
         a. Investment Tax Credits (“ITCs”) for the Cunningham and Plant X battery
            projects, which SPS will amortize over ﬁve years to reduce its revenue
            requirement. SPS will apply a return on the unamortized balance of the
            monetized ITC at its proposed 8.21 percent WACC, and SPS will recover any
            transfer costs, capped at ten percent of each ITC’s nominal value, through
            amortization over the same period as the ITC and apply a return on the
            unamortized balance at its proposed 8.21 percent WACC;
        b. Production Tax Credits (“PTCs”) from SPS solar facilities, the value of which
            SPS has been authorized to provide to customers through the FPPCAC along
            with transfer costs, will be recorded in a Deferred Tax Asset (“DTA”) to the
            extent they are unused or not yet transferred with a return at the same cost of
            capital recovered through base rates; and
        c. PTC transfer costs for the Hale and Sagamore wind facilities;
10. Authorize cost recovery mechanisms to address variable costs, including:
        a. a property tax tracker for expenses above the Future Test Year baseline;
        b. an Excess Liability Insurance (“ELI”) expense tracker consistent with the
            Commission’s Final Order in Case No. 25-00030-UT;
        c. recovery of SPS’s Southwest Power Pool deﬁciency payments through the Fuel
            and Purchased Power Cost Adjustment Clause (“FPPCAC”);
11. Approve SPS’s request to recover previously approved regulatory assets and ﬁxed
    deferrals, including:
        a. a two-year amortization of deferred Excess Liability Insurance (“ELI”)
            premiums (Case No. 25-00030-UT);
        b. a two-year amortization of the remaining investment in legacy meters (Case
            No. 22-00178-UT); and
        c. recovery of Community Solar Program costs, including regulatory and
            information technology expenses (Case No. 23-00071-UT);
12. Permit SPS to retain 10% of off-system sales margins from the Cunningham and Plant
    X Solar Projects;
13. Approve SPS’s rate case and other regulatory expenses, including recovery of
    deferred expenses from prior proceedings;
14. Approve SPS’s Electric Affordability Program to assist income-eligible residential
    customers under NMSA 1978, § 62-8-6 (2025);
15. Approve SPS’s proposed rate design and cost allocation, including its proposed
    jurisdictional allocation.
16. Set a public hearing concerning the justness and reasonableness of SPS’s proposed
    rates; and



                                          -3-
    17. Grant all other approvals, authorizations, and variances that the Commission
       determines are necessary for SPS to effectuate and implement the relief granted in
       this case.

The proposed rate changes will affect all retail customers and customer classifications. The
present and proposed rates for each customer class proposed by SPS are provided in the
QR Code.

The proposed changes in rates stated by class and by consumption levels are for
informational purposes only and the final rate design may vary the rates ultimately charged
to each class and for each consumption level.

                           Scan to view SPS’s proposed rates




                                 https://www.prc.nm.gov

SPS also is proposing to modify the following rate tariff provisions:
           a) Rate Nos. 1 and 39, Residential Service and Residential Heating Service –
              update Service Availability Charges (to 75% of allocated class cost of service
              where applicable), revise seasonal and Time-of-Use energy charges to reﬂect
              proposed rates, and shift summer On-Peak Hours from 12 p.m.–6 p.m.
              weekdays to 1 p.m.–8 p.m. daily;
           b) Rate No. 3, Irrigation Power Service – update Service Availability, demand, and
              Time-of-Use energy charges to reﬂect proposed rates and shift summer On-
              Peak Hours to 1 p.m.–8 p.m. daily;
           c) Rate No. 6, Small General Service – revise Applicability, update Service
              Availability Charges (including Optional Unmetered Service), revise seasonal
                                              -4-
    and Time-of-Use energy charges to reﬂect proposed rates, and shift summer
   On-Peak Hours to 1 p.m.–8 p.m. daily;
d) Rate Nos. 13 and 40, Primary General Service and Secondary General Service
   – revise Applicability where applicable, update Service Availability and energy
   charges, restructure Demand Charges into separate Distribution Demand and
   seasonal Generation & Transmission Demand components, modify Power
   Factor Adjustment charges, and discontinue Power Factor credits;
e) Rate Nos. 14 and 28, Municipal Street Lighting Service and Area Lighting
   Service – update monthly rates per lamp type/size and per-kWh rates for
   customer-owned systems to reﬂect proposed rates;
f) Rate Nos. 16 and 42, Large Municipal and School Service and Small Municipal
   and School Service – revise Applicability, update Service Availability, demand,
   and Time-of-Use energy charges to reﬂect proposed rates, shift summer On-
   Peak Hours to 1 p.m.–8 p.m. daily, update optional unmetered service rates
   where applicable, modify Power Factor Adjustment charges, and discontinue
   Power Factor credits;
g) Rate No. 26, Miscellaneous Service Charges – update Returned Check, After-
   Hours Connection, Reconnect, Special Bill Form, Restoration of Tampered
   Service, Account History, Out-of-Cycle Meter Reading, and Switchover Policy
   charges to reﬂect proposed rates;
h) Rate No. 27, SLCA Integrated Projects Energy Rider for Cannon Air Force Base
   – update Energy and Demand Credits, and revise SPS loss percentage;
i) Rate No. 34, Large General Service – Transmission – update Service
   Availability, energy, and seasonal demand charges for both Sub-Transmission
   (69 kV) and Backbone Transmission (115 kV and above), revise Determination
   of Demand provisions, modify Power Factor Adjustment charges, and
   discontinue Power Factor credits;
j) Rate No. 72, Fuel and Purchased Power Cost Adjustment Clause – add
   provisions for an Optional Time-of-Use Pilot Rate (including Applicability,
   Availability, On-Peak/Off-Peak hours, and Monthly Rate);

                                 -5-
           k) Rate No. 73, General Service – Time of Use Rate – revise Applicability, update
             Service Availability, On-Peak/Off-Peak energy, Distribution Demand, and
             Transmission Demand charges to reﬂect proposed rates, shift summer On-
             Peak Hours to 1 p.m.–8 p.m. daily, and modify Power Factor charges;
          l) Rate No. 85, Standby Service Rider – shift summer On-Peak Hours to 1 p.m.–8
             p.m. daily, revise Supplementary Power terms, update Service Availability and
             Meter Charges, revise standby generation/transmission reservation and
             energy charges (seasonally differentiated where applicable) under both
             Option 1 and Option 2 for 69 kV and 115 kV-and-above classes, and modify
             Power Factor charges;
          m) Rate No. 87, Community Solar Program Credit Rider – revise Solar Bill Credit
             Rate calculations and components, add 69 kV and 115 kV-and-above
             transmission classes to credit tables, and update Appendix A CSP
             Component Costs per kWh;
          n) Rate No. 89, Electric Affordability Program – new rider (substantially
             unchanged from prior New Mexico rate case) to mitigate bill impacts for
             qualiﬁed low-income residential customers;
          o) Rate No. 91, Large Customer RenewableConnect Rate Rider – revise summer
             and winter RenewableConnect Unbundled Production Credits; and
          p) Finally, SPS is proposing a modiﬁcation to Rule No. 16, Extensions to
             Customers. Speciﬁcally, SPS is proposing updates to the line extension policy
             to better align with modern infrastructure needs, improve coordination with
             third-party vendors, enhance wildﬁre mitigation efforts, and ensure equitable
             cost distribution.


                                  PUBLIC HEARING
A public hearing will be held beginning at 9:00 a.m. on May 26, 2026, and will continue
through June 5, 2026. The public hearing is where the Commission receives testimony,
exhibits, and legal arguments about the Application. Members of the public can watch the
hearing via a livestream on the Commission’s YouTube channel and its website,


                                           -6-
 https://www.prc.nm.gov/public-hearings/. Please contact the Commission for
confirmation of the hearing because hearings are occasionally cancelled or rescheduled.

                                 PUBLIC COMMENT
If you are interested in the case but do not wish to become a party, you may make oral or
written comment as allowed by Rule 1.2.2.23(F) NMAC. The Commission will host a public
comment session at which members of the public may make comments in person. The date,
time, and place of the public comment session will be announced on the Commission’s
website.

Public comment can be provided at Commission open meetings. The open meetings
schedule is available on the Commission website at www.prc.nm.gov/nmprc-open-
meeting-agenda/.

Public comment will not be taken at the evidentiary hearing because comments are not
evidence. You may send written comments before the Commission takes final action by
sending the comment, which must specifically reference Case No. 25-00079-UT, to
prc.records@prc.nm.gov, or Commission Records Management Bureau, P.O. Box 1269,
Santa Fe, NM 87504. The Commission may be reached by telephone at 1-888-427-5772.
